rubric.why: Award for using the Kelvin-to-Celsius relation and obtaining the Celsius temperature.

rubric.how: Award for stating the answer in degrees Celsius.

modelAnswer: Given: T = 900 K
Formula: T(°C) = T(K) − 273
Substitution: T(°C) = 900 − 273
Answer: T = 627 °C.

items.followUp: Define centrifugal force and give one example.

rubric.why: This is the defining direction of centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the force acts towards the centre of the circular path.

rubric.why: A relevant example demonstrates the concept.
rubric.how: Award for one valid example of centripetal force.

rubric.why: This is the centripetal acceleration used in the derivation.
rubric.how: Award for writing the relation between centripetal acceleration, speed and radius.

rubric.why: This is the required formula for centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award for using F = ma to obtain the centripetal-force formula.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force is the force that keeps a body moving in a circular path and is directed towards the centre of the circle.
Example: The tension in a string provides the centripetal force when a stone is whirled in a circle.
For a body moving in a circle of radius r with speed v, its centripetal acceleration is a = v²/r.
By Newton’s second law, F = ma.
Therefore, F = m(v²/r) = mv²/r.

items.followUp: State Pascal’s law and derive the equation relating the forces and piston areas in a hydraulic machine.

accept: pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally
rubric.why: This is the principle underlying the hydraulic press.
rubric.how: Award for stating that applied pressure is transmitted equally throughout the enclosed liquid.

rubric.why: Pressure at the small piston is force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award for correctly expressing pressure at the first piston.

rubric.why: Pressure at the large piston is force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award for correctly expressing pressure at the second piston.

rubric.why: Equating the pressures gives the hydraulic-press equation.
rubric.how: Award for equating the pressures and obtaining the force-area relation.

modelAnswer: Pascal’s law states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions.
Let F₁ and A₁ be the force and area of the small piston, and F₂ and A₂ those of the large piston.
Pressure on the small piston: P₁ = F₁/A₁.
Pressure on the large piston: P₂ = F₂/A₂.
By Pascal’s law, P₁ = P₂, so F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂.
Therefore, F₂/F₁ = A₂/A₁, or F₂ = F₁A₂/A₁.

items.followUp: A cyclist starts from rest and accelerates at 0.8 m s⁻² over 50 m. Find the final speed in km h⁻¹.

rubric.why: Correct identification of the initial speed, acceleration and distance is needed for substitution.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the relevant quantities in SI units.

rubric.why: This motion equation relates final speed to acceleration and distance without requiring time.
rubric.how: Award for selecting the correct equation.

rubric.why: Correct substitution gives 10 m s⁻¹.
rubric.description: Substitution and speed in SI units
rubric.how: Award for substituting correctly and finding the speed in m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: The requested final answer is in km h⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award for converting 10 m s⁻¹ to 36 km h⁻¹.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 0 m s⁻¹, a = 0.5 m s⁻², s = 100 m
Formula: v² = u² + 2as
Substitution: v² = (0 m s⁻¹)² + 2(0.5 m s⁻²)(100 m) = 100 m² s⁻²
Therefore, v = 10 m s⁻¹.
Conversion: 10 × 3.6 = 36 km h⁻¹
Answer: The train’s speed is 36 km h⁻¹.

items.followUp: A force has perpendicular components of 6 N east and 8 N north. Find its magnitude and direction using the head-to-tail rule.

rubric.why: The first component must be represented as the starting vector.
rubric.how: Award for describing or showing the first component drawn from a chosen starting point.

rubric.why: The second component must be placed perpendicular to the first at its head.
rubric.how: Award for placing the second component at the head of the first and at right angles.

rubric.why: For perpendicular components, the resultant magnitude follows from Pythagoras’ theorem.
rubric.how: Award for the correct magnitude relation.

rubric.why: This gives the direction of the resultant relative to the first component.
rubric.how: Award for the correct direction relation.

modelAnswer: Let the perpendicular components be Fₓ and Fᵧ.
Draw Fₓ from a chosen starting point; from its head draw Fᵧ at right angles to Fₓ.
The resultant R is drawn from the tail of Fₓ to the head of Fᵧ.
Because the components are perpendicular, R = √(Fₓ² + Fᵧ²).
The direction θ measured from Fₓ is given by tan θ = Fᵧ/Fₓ, so θ = tan⁻¹(Fᵧ/Fₓ).

items.followUp: A vehicle weighs 10 kN and travels at 15 m s⁻¹. Find its kinetic energy. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The weight must be converted to newtons before finding the mass.
rubric.how: Award for identifying 12 kN as 12,000 N.

rubric.why: Using W = mg gives the car’s mass.
rubric.how: Award for correctly finding the mass using g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: This is the kinetic-energy formula.
rubric.how: Award for writing the correct formula.

rubric.why: Correct substitution and evaluation give the kinetic energy in joules.
rubric.how: Award for substituting the mass and speed and obtaining 2.4 × 10⁵ J.

modelAnswer: Given: Weight W = 12 kN = 12,000 N; speed v = 20 m s⁻¹; take g = 10 m s⁻².
Formula for weight: W = mg.
Formula for kinetic energy: KE = ½mv².
Substitution: KE = ½(1,200 kg)(20 m s⁻¹)².

modelAnswer: A screw gauge is a precision instrument used to measure small dimensions, such as the diameter of a thin wire or the thickness of a sheet.
The pitch of a screw gauge is the distance moved by its screw along its axis in one complete rotation.
